主要内容: Mallinckrodt Pharmaceuticals reported first-quarter 2019 earnings that exceeded expectations, generating $790.6 million in revenue, surpassing the estimated $767.2 million. The company attributed its strong performance to sales of hospital products and generic drugs. CEO Mark Trudeau highlighted the company's continued strong operational execution and growth. Mallinckrodt also raised its sales projections for specialty generic drugs, expecting growth of 2% to 5%, up from its original guidance of 1% to 4%. The company raised its 2019 adjusted earnings guidance to $8.30 to $8.60 per share, up from $8.10 to $8.40. Despite the positive earnings, the company faces two whistleblower lawsuits that have impacted its stock. Mallinckrodt expects to complete the separation of its Specialty Generics and Amitiza segment by the second half of 2019. The generics segment reported net sales of $243.3 million, up 17.6% year over year, while Amitiza sales increased by 3.5% to $53 million. However, sales of H.P. Acthar Gel, one of the company's best-performing drugs, fell 8.2% to $223.9 million, though the company still expects sales to exceed $1 billion for the year. Mallinckrodt, a pharmaceutical company, is facing lawsuits related to its 2014 acquisition of Questcor Pharmaceuticals. The lawsuits allege that Questcor bribed doctors to prescribe its drug and defrauded Medicare by illegally marketing H.P. Acthar Gel. The Department of Justice intervened in April after an investigation. During a shareholder conference call, Mallinckrodt's CEO, Trudeau, stated the company is working diligently to resolve the lawsuits, which were filed in 2012 and 2013. He emphasized that while the company disagrees with the complaints, it is seeking a reasonable resolution. H.P. Acthar Gel saw a sharp price increase in 2007, with the price of one vial rising from $2,000 to $28,000, now exceeding $40,000. Analysts at Mizuho noted that the miss in net sales for Acthar Gel was already priced into the stock, though it remains a key driver during earnings.
